description: Browse fused.catalog collections, preview one on a map over time and copy the code that reads it

catalog.description: The fused.catalog reader whose collections show first: "imagery". Defaults to "imagery".

collection.description: A collection to open on load, by id (e.g. "hls2-s30"). Accepts a $param reference. Omit it to start on the list of collections.

param.description: Canvas parameter the widget writes with what the open collection shows: { collection, bounds: [west, south, east, north] or the drawn GeoJSON polygon, time: "start/end" or null, bands: [...], mask_clouds, and composite and reducer when one is picked }. A UDF downstream can pass it to fused.catalog.imagery.

style.description: CSS string for the outer element.

propsSchema.description:
Browses the datasets fused.catalog serves and previews one. The list shows every collection with a thumbnail, its resolution, time range and bands, by category and search. Opening a collection draws its pixels over the map view straight from the reader (no UDF runs), steps through the scenes of a date range (the last 6 months of a time series by default) on a time bar with the band's mean over time, and gives the UDF code that reads the same area, dates and bands, ready to copy. The Output toggle (Pixels / H3) switches both the map and the code: H3 draws the reader's H3 cells at the data's resolution (the coarsest whose cells are no larger than a pixel: 12 for 30 m, 13 for 10 m), and the code passes that h3_res. Composite (None by default; Daily, Monthly, Yearly or Full range, by Median, Mean, Min, Max, First or Last) has the reader reduce the scenes to one image per period, and the code passes that composite and reducer. The pencil under the zoom buttons draws a polygon (click its points, then double-click or click the first point; Esc cancels): the reader reads only inside it instead of the map view, and the code passes that geometry; the bin clears it and goes back to the view. The code always reads what Run loads. The basemap is Map or Satellite. Auto-run is off by default: the opening view loads, then Run loads the current view (a zoomed-in part of the loaded area too), or every pan, zoom or setting change loads straight away once Auto-run is on; the dotted outline marks the loaded area.

## Example

```json
{ "type": "data-catalog", "props": { "style": "height: 720px" } }
```

Open one collection and share what it shows:

```json
{ "type": "data-catalog", "props": { "collection": "hls2-s30", "param": "imagery" } }
```
